_meta.indication: AVYCAZ (ceftazidime-avibactam) is indicated in patients 18 years or older, in combination with metronidazole, for complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) and for complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis, caused by designated susceptible microorganisms; reserve for use in patients who have limited or no alternative treatment options

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, multicenter, investigator-blinded, randomized trial of ceftazidime-avibactam versus imipenem-cilastatin; randomized 1:1
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Microbiological and clinical outcome at the Test of Cure (TOC) visit in the mMITT population (no formal hypothesis for inferential testing was prespecified)
pivotal_trials.n: 135 randomized (68 ceftazidime-avibactam, 67 imipenem-cilastatin); mMITT N=46 vs N=49
pivotal_trials.result: Favorable microbiological response (eradication) 67.4% vs 63.3% (difference 4.1; 95% CI -16.1, 23.8); clinical cure 80.4% vs 73.5% (difference 7.0; 95% CI -11.6, 24.7); no inferential testing prespecified so no definitive efficacy conclusion

nct_ctgov.title: Comparative Study of NXL104/Ceftazidime Versus Comparator in Adults With Complicated Urinary Tract Infections

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized 1:1 trial of ceftazidime-avibactam plus metronidazole versus meropenem
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical outcome at the Test of Cure (TOC) visit in the mMITT population (no formal hypothesis for inferential testing was prespecified)
pivotal_trials.n: 204 randomized (102 ceftazidime-avibactam plus metronidazole, 102 meropenem); mMITT N=85 vs N=89
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical response at TOC (mMITT) 82.4% (70/85) ceftazidime-avibactam plus metronidazole vs 88.8% (79/89) meropenem (observed difference -6.4; 95% CI -18.0, 5.2); no inferential testing prespecified

nct_ctgov.title: Prospective Multicenter Doubleblind Randomized Study of NXL104/Ceftazidime + Metronidazole vs. Meropenem in Treatment of Complicated Intra-abdominal Infections

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10% in either indication) are vomiting, nausea, constipation, and anxiety; in the Phase 3 cIAI trial death occurred in 2.5% (13/529) of AVYCAZ/metronidazole vs 1.5% (8/529) meropenem, and in patients with baseline CrCL 30-50 mL/min death occurred in 25.8% (8/31) vs 8.6% (3/35)
target_moa: Ceftazidime is a cephalosporin whose bactericidal action is mediated by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); avibactam is a non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor that inactivates some beta-lactamases and protects ceftazidime from degradation
modality: Small molecule combination (third-generation cephalosporin plus non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor)

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (December 5, 2014): cIAI indication Yes 11 / No 1; cUTI indication Yes 9 / No 3

summary.text: AVYCAZ was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA relying in part on FDA's prior finding of safety and efficacy of ceftazidime, with efficacy based on two Phase 2 trials (cUTI and cIAI) plus supportive in vitro/animal and limited Phase 3 data; the product held QIDP and fast track designations (granted March 11, 2013) and received priority review under GAIN, and was approved February 25, 2015 (not under accelerated approval)
